name: North Carolina
verdict: Its 340B hospitals cleared $4.1 billion in a year and take an estimated $1.1 billion in tax breaks. A physician still needs a state permit to open a competing facility.

grade.note: Driver grades are the Rojas Report editorial grades from Build Brief 2 (November 6, 2026), provisional until the state-grade rubric is published at /methodology/state-grade/.

money.asOf: North Carolina's 54 hospitals in the 340B program, fiscal years ending 2024 to 2025

items.text: in net income in one year, on $36.7B of patient revenue.
items.note: 48 of 54 made money. CMS hospital cost reports, latest report per hospital.

items.text: a year in estimated tax breaks, against $846M of charity care.
items.note: Federal income $862M, state income $92M, property $161M, at 2025 rates. Sales tax not estimated.
items.source: Rojas Report North Carolina state dossier, release r71 (October 13, 2026), section 5: federal income tax $862,401,207 (21% of cost-report net income of the 48 profitable hospitals), North Carolina income tax $92,400,129 (2.25% rate, tax year 2025), property tax high case $161,322,797 (commercial effective rates from the Lincoln Institute / Minnesota Center for Fiscal Excellence 50-State Property Tax Comparison Study, April 2026 edition, taxes paid in 2025, on $18.4 billion of land and buildings at historical cost); total $1,116,124,133. Charity care at cost 846,319,513 from the cost reports
items.as_of: exemptions at 2025 rates on hospital fiscal years ending 2024 to 2025

items.text: 340B contract pharmacy arrangements with pharmacies outside North Carolina, of 1,698 in all.
items.source: HRSA 340B OPAIS export of September 29, 2026: 1,698 active contract pharmacy arrangements for the 54 hospitals, 770 with pharmacies outside the state (45%)

drivers.label: Section 6001
drivers.title: Physician-owned hospitals
drivers.body: The federal ban applies here as everywhere. North Carolina has one physician-owned hospital left, North Carolina Specialty Hospital in Durham, grandfathered under Section 6001. No new one can open and bill Medicare.
drivers.source: Rojas Report physician-owned hospital database (Physician_Owned_Hospitals_US.xlsx, February 2026): master list row 78, North Carolina Specialty Hospital, Durham, grandfathered (ACA Section 6001), operating; summary by state NC 1 listed, 1 operating

drivers.label: Price Transparency
drivers.title: Prices without teeth
drivers.body: No North Carolina hospital price-disclosure statute beyond the federal rule has been found yet. Two 2025 bills, HB 434 and SB 316 (Lower Healthcare Costs), name price transparency. HB 434 sits in conference and SB 316 in House Health.
drivers.status: PENDING RESEARCH · State statute review open
drivers.source: Rojas Report North Carolina state dossier, release r71 (October 13, 2026), section 7: bill-text search for 'price transparency', 2025-2026 Session (HB 434 passed both chambers in 2025, House failed to concur June 17, 2025, conferees changed April 6, 2026; SB 316 passed the Senate March 27, 2025, re-referred to House Health May 6, 2026); no state statute reviewed

drivers.label: Certificate of Need
drivers.title: Still a permit to compete
drivers.body: CON remains law under G.S. 131E Article 9. Session Law 2023-7 trimmed it: psychiatric and chemical dependency facilities are out, and urban surgery centers in counties over 125,000 are exempt. MRI review narrows to smaller counties in a later stage. New hospitals and acute-care beds still need state approval.
drivers.linkText: Read the North Carolina CON brief
drivers.source: Rojas Report North Carolina state dossier, release r71 (October 13, 2026), section 4: G.S. 131E-176(9b) scope; Session Law 2023-7 (HB 76) sections 3.1 (diagnostic threshold $1.5M to $3M, psychiatric and chemical dependency beds), 3.2 (psychiatric and chemical dependency facilities out; qualified urban ambulatory surgical facilities in counties over 125,000 exempt, G.S. 131E-147.5 4% rule, in effect two years after the first HASP payment) and 3.3 (MRI review limited to counties of 125,000 or fewer, three years after the first HASP payment)

drivers.label: Hospital Subsidies
drivers.title: $1.1 billion a year in tax breaks
drivers.body: Estimated federal, state and property tax exemptions for the 54 hospitals in the 340B program come to $1.1 billion a year. Against that, $846 million of charity care at cost. Those hospitals run 855 340B child sites and 1,698 contract pharmacy arrangements.
drivers.source: Rojas Report North Carolina state dossier, release r71 (October 13, 2026), section 5 (exemptions $1,116,124,133 at 2025 rates; charity care at cost 846,319,513); HRSA 340B OPAIS export of September 29, 2026 (855 child sites, 1,698 arrangements); SB 517 in Senate Rules and Operations since March 26, 2025

drivers.label: CMS Favoritism
drivers.title: Urban hospitals, rural rules
drivers.body: 12 of the 54 are hospitals in urban areas that CMS treats as rural under 42 CFR 412.103. Duke University Hospital, UNC Hospitals and Novant Health New Hanover are among them. Rural status can lower the 340B eligibility bar for a rural referral center and change Medicare wage-index reclassification.
drivers.source: Rojas Report North Carolina state dossier, release r71 (October 13, 2026), section 4: 12 of 54 with dual classification (cost report Rural; CMS FY2027 IPPS impact file urban, Section 401 flag): Duke Regional, Forsyth Memorial, Cape Fear Valley Medical Center, Catawba Valley, Moses H Cone Memorial, Alamance Regional, Duke University Hospital, FirstHealth Moore Regional, Novant Health New Hanover, Onslow Memorial, UNC Hospitals, Wayne Memorial
drivers.as_of: CMS FY2027 IPPS final rule impact file (correction notice)

drivers.label: Stark & Anti-Kickback
drivers.title: No room to build rivals
drivers.body: Whether North Carolina self-referral and anti-kickback law goes beyond the federal statutes is not yet researched.

rows.title: Cap hospital 340B payments at cost
rows.body: Would cap what a 340B hospital accepts for a 340B drug at its acquisition cost and require annual 340B reporting to the state.

rows.title: Pharmacy benefit manager provisions
rows.body: Pharmacy benefit manager bill with 340B provisions. Passed the House 106 to 9 in April 2025 and sits in Senate Rules.

rows.title: SB 479, the SCRIPT Act
rows.body: Bars pharmacy benefit managers from discriminating against 340B entities and their contract pharmacies.

rows.title: Medicaid expansion and CON reform
rows.body: Expanded Medicaid and phased out parts of certificate of need: one change on enactment, two more tied to the first hospital directed payment.
